title: Troubleshoot alarm 9973 incoming power fault on a Haas machine
scope: Alarm 9973 troubleshooting as demonstrated in SRC_HAAS_0011.

context.subsystem: incoming power monitoring (Wye-Delta contactor and I/O PCB)
symptoms: alarm 9973 on screen and machine stops

subsystem.note: Named in the narration and the official description.

alarm_codes.note: Stated in the narration, the title card and the control banner.

components.note: Named in the narration or shown with labels on screen.

steps.title: Understand alarm 9973 and how the machine monitors incoming power

context.text: The presenter says the 9973 alarm tells you there is a problem with the incoming power supplied to the machine.
context.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

context.text: A title card reads 'ALARM 9973 - INVALID POWER CONTROL STATE DETECTED'.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Title card: 'HAAS AUTOMATION SERVICE VIDEO - ALARM 9973 - INVALID POWER CONTROL STATE DETECTED'.
evidence.explanation: The card text is legible in the frame.

context.explanation: The presenter names the alarm and its subject at the start of the video.

rationale.text: The presenter says the Wye-Delta contactor has one set of contacts closed and the other open at all times, and that power from the I/O board keeps the relevant contactor closed and conducting current.
rationale.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

rationale.text: The presenter says that in a brownout the power keeping the contactor closed might sag momentarily and let the contactor open, and that if this happens under full load the contactor will arc and can cause serious damage.

The presenter says that all Wye-Delta contactor assemblies built after August 2017 use a pair of auxiliary contacts to monitor the open and closed state of the main contacts, and that a cable connects these auxiliary contacts to the I/O PCB so the machine can check the contactor status continuously.
rationale.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

observation.text: The presenter says a 9973 alarm means the I/O board saw one of these contacts open when it should have been closed, and that the alarm shows on screen and the machine stops.
observation.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

observation.text: A close-up of a contactor block carries the overlay label 'AUXILIARY CONTACTS'.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Close-up of a contactor block with the overlay label 'AUXILIARY CONTACTS'.
evidence.explanation: The overlay label is legible in the frame.

observation.explanation: The narration at this moment is about the auxiliary contacts and their cable.

observation.text: The control shows a red banner for alarm 9973 whose visible text includes 'INVALID POWE' (the end is cut off).

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Control screen with a red banner for alarm 9973 whose visible text includes 'INVALID POWE' (the end is cut off).
evidence.explanation: The banner text is partly legible; the end of the line is cut off at the screen edge.

observation.explanation: The narration at this moment is about the alarm appearing on screen.

questions.question: The title card says 'Invalid power control state detected' while the YouTube title says 'Unstable incoming power'; which wording does the control use?

steps.title: Power down safely before opening anything

action.text: The presenter says to power down the machine and wait for the vector drive caution light to go dark.
The POWER ON and POWER OFF buttons are shown under the caption 'ALARM 9973 - POWER DOWN THE MACHINE. WAIT UNTIL VECTOR DRIVE LIGHT TURNS OFF.'

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: POWER ON and POWER OFF buttons with the caption 'ALARM 9973 - POWER DOWN THE MACHINE. WAIT UNTIL VECTOR DRIVE LIGHT TURNS OFF.'
evidence.explanation: The caption text and the buttons are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about powering down.

rationale.text: The presenter says that once the light is dark there is no residual energy left in the system.
A vector drive label reads 'DANGER! High voltage! No user serviceable parts inside. Light must be out before replacing drive.'

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Vector drive label 'DANGER! High voltage! No user serviceable parts inside. Light must be out before replacing drive' with the same caption.
evidence.explanation: The warning label is legible in the frame.

rationale.explanation: The narration at this moment is about waiting for the drive light to go out.

questions.question: How long should the wait be? The video says to wait for the light, with no time.

steps.title: Remove the covers and check the connections

action.text: The presenter says to remove the covers from the Wye-Delta contactor and the I/O PCB.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description). The caption writes 'Y Delta'; the on-screen caption and the description write 'Wye/Delta'.

action.text: Hands remove a metal cover under the caption 'ALARM 9973 - REMOVE COVERS FROM THE WYE/DELTA CONTRACTOR AND I/O PCB.'

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Hands removing a metal cover; caption 'ALARM 9973 - REMOVE COVERS FROM THE WYE/DELTA CONTRACTOR AND I/O PCB.'
evidence.explanation: The caption text and the hands removing the cover are visible in the frame; the caption spells 'contractor'.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about removing the covers.

action.text: The presenter says to verify that the cable from the Wye-Delta auxiliary contacts is connected to the I/O PCB correctly, and that there is no arcing at the Wye-Delta connections or the vector drive connections.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. The caption writes 'Y Delta'; the on-screen caption and the description write 'Wye/Delta'.

action.text: Two stacked contactors and a terminal block are shown under the caption about the auxiliary contacts being connected to the I/O PCB and no arcing.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Two stacked contactors and a terminal block; caption about the Wye/Delta auxiliary contacts being connected to the I/O PCB and no arcing.
evidence.explanation: The contactors, terminal block and caption are visible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about verifying the cable and checking for arcing.

acceptance_criteria.text: The presenter says that if everything checks out, the problem was likely a brownout where insufficient incoming power was supplied.

questions.question: What does arcing look like, and what is done if it is found? The video only says to check for it.

steps.title: Conclude brownout and stabilize the incoming power

outcome.text: The presenter says that in this case the I/O board did its job and protected the contactors from a dangerous arc.
outcome.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

condition.text: The presenter says this applies if the 9973 alarm is persistent.
condition.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

action.text: The presenter says a persistent 9973 alarm means the machine needs a third-party power conditioner or voltage stabilizer installed on the incoming power line.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

action.text: The presenter says not to change the Wye-Delta assembly or the I/O PCB.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. The caption words the assembly as 'delta Y assembly'. The caption writes 'Y Delta'; the on-screen caption and the description write 'Wye/Delta'.

rationale.text: The presenter says recurring 9973 alarms very likely mean problems with the incoming power supply, and that stabilizing the power reaching the machine will make these alarms go away.
rationale.explanation: The captions state this directly. The caption splits the number across cues ('9 9 7' / '3 alarms'); the claim reads it as 9973 per the video's title. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

questions.question: Who selects and installs the power conditioner, and to what specification? The video does not say.

steps.title: Special cases: logged-only alarms and machines without the monitoring hardware

condition.text: The presenter says this applies if an alarm is logged into history but did not appear on screen or stop the machine.
condition.explanation: The captions state this directly. The caption reads 'alarm 973', which is probably 9973 but is not corrected here.

condition.text: The presenter says this applies if the machine does not have the Wye-Delta auxiliary contacts and the extra cable.
condition.explanation: The captions state this directly. The caption writes 'Y Delta'; the on-screen caption and the description write 'Wye/Delta'.

action.text: The presenter says to ignore such an alarm.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. The sentence continues with a garbled mention of an upgrade to the software version shown on screen.

action.text: The presenter says the power monitoring feature should not be enabled on a machine without the auxiliary contacts and extra cable, and to make sure the correct configuration file is loaded in the machine.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).

context.text: The presenter says that for more in-depth Wye-Delta contactor troubleshooting, to click the links in the description, which lead to a DIY site.
context.explanation: The captions state this directly. Cue 25 is corrected from 'why delta contact or' to 'Wye-Delta contactor'; the web address in cues 25-26 is garbled and is not repeated. The official description does link a Haas DIY Wye-Delta contactor guide.

questions.question: The captions mention an upgrade to the software version shown on screen right after 'ignore the alarm'. Is the upgrade a second instruction or part of the ignore case?
Which alarm number is logged but not shown: 9973 or a different one? The caption reads 973.

claim.text: The presenter has the machine powered down and the drive light out before the covers come off.
The presenter makes the power conditioner recommendation conditional on the 9973 alarm being persistent.
claim.explanation: The captions state this directly. Corrected cues: '997 three alarm' to '9973 alarm' (the video's title) and 'wide delta' to 'Wye-Delta' (the description).
